summary: The S&P 500 topped 7,300 for the first time ever, capping a six-week winning streak driven by a furious AI and semiconductor surge. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index traded higher for 18 straight trading days, rising 47%, as markets actively reward physical chip manufacturing capacity, treating semiconductor infrastructure as the defining asset of the cycle.
tweet: The S&P 500 hit a record 7,300+ on a six-week streak, led by memory stocks — the Roundhill Memory ETF soared nearly 30% in one week — while the Trump-Xi summit puts Iran and trade squarely in the spotlight.
